mainTopic: The daily and שבת songs of the לוים in the מקדש, and the ten stages in which the שכינה and the סנהדרין went into exile
overview: This amud opens by rejecting a proof about what the לוים sang on a day of doubt, because in that case the psalm fit either way. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא listing the שיר של יום for each day of the week, each tied to what God did on that day of Creation. רבי עקיבא explains the שבת psalm as being about a future 'day that is all שבת.' רבי נחמיה objects and says it is about God resting at Creation, and the גמרא links their argument to רב קטינא and אביי on how long the world will be destroyed. Next we learn the special songs for שבת: האזינו in six parts at מוסף, and שירת הים and שירת הבאר at מנחה, with one part sung each week. רבי יוחנן then teaches that the שכינה left the מקדש in ten stages, and the גמרא proves each stage from a פסוק. It waited six months in the wilderness hoping for תשובה. Finally, the סנהדרין was exiled in ten matching stages, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: That case proves nothing, since the psalm fit either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof. In that case the psalm sung (״הרנינו״) was the correct שיר של יום no matter how the doubt was resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because that psalm was the song of the day anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on a proof brought on the previous amud. It says that case is special, so we cannot learn a general rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof wanted to show that on an uncertain day the לוים sang the ordinary weekday psalm. The rejection points out that in that case, the psalm sung was correct whether the day was treated as an ordinary Thursday or as ראש השנה. So there was no real doubt to resolve. We still do not know what they did in a truly uncertain case; maybe they sang nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; a standard phrase for rejecting a proof by showing the case is special
Song, meaning the psalm the לוים sang with the קרבן
Of its day; the psalm assigned to that specific day

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not say the לוים definitely sang the weekday psalm. It only says this particular case cannot prove it, because the psalm fit both possibilities.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: Rejecting the proof from the case just cited

phrases.english: because it is the song of its day.
phrases.notes: The psalm was correct either way, so no proof

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought at the end of the previous section (on the previous amud)
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The underlying question about what was sung on an uncertain day stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cited case had no real doubt, because the psalm sung was the שיר של יום under both possibilities.

steps.title: Sunday's psalm: The earth is God's
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי יהודה in the name of רבי עקיבא teaches that on Sunday the לוים sang ״לה׳ הארץ ומלואה״. On the first day God owned the world, gave it over, and ruled it alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי עקיבא: On the first day, what would they say? "The earth is the Lord's and its fullness," because He acquired, gave over, and ruled alone in His world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא that goes through the psalm the לוים sang on each day of the week. Here it gives Sunday's psalm and the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each daily psalm matches what God did on that day of Creation. On day one God created the world and owned it. He was the only ruler, because the angels were not created until day two. That is why the psalm declares that the whole earth belongs to God.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the שיר של יום that we still say every day at the end of שחרית.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says
phrases.notes: Introducing a ברייתא

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
On the first day, what would they say?
phrases.notes: The לוים in the מקדש

phrases.english: "The earth is the Lord's and its fullness"
phrases.notes: תהלים כ״ד

phrases.english: because He acquired and gave over
phrases.notes: He owned the world and transferred it to mankind

phrases.english: and ruled alone in His world.
phrases.notes: The angels did not yet exist

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the uncertain-day discussion to a full list of the daily psalms
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Sunday the לוים sang ״לה׳ הארץ ומלואה״, recalling God's sole ownership and rule on the first day of Creation.

steps.title: Monday's psalm: Great is God
steps.stepSummary: On Monday the לוים sang ״גדול ה׳ ומהולל מאד״. On the second day God separated His creations and ruled over them as King.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second day, what would they say? "Great is the Lord and highly praised," because He divided His works and ruled over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with Monday's psalm and its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On day two God split the upper waters from the lower waters, separating His creations. Ruling over separate domains is a picture of kingship. This psalm praises God as the great King in Jerusalem.

keyTerms.meaning: He divided His works (the upper and lower waters)

phrases.english: On the second day, what would they say?
"Great is the Lord and highly praised"
phrases.notes: תהלים מ״ח

phrases.english: because He divided His works
phrases.notes: The upper and lower waters

phrases.english: and reigned over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of daily psalms
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Monday the לוים sang ״גדול ה׳״, recalling God's separating the waters and ruling over them.

steps.title: Tuesday's psalm: God stands in His congregation
steps.stepSummary: On Tuesday the לוים sang ״אלהים נצב בעדת אל״. On the third day God revealed dry land and prepared the world for His people.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the third day they would say: "God stands in the congregation of God," because He revealed the land in His wisdom and prepared the world for His congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives Tuesday's psalm and its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On day three the waters gathered and dry land appeared. That made the world livable for people, the "congregation" who would stand before God. The psalm speaks of God standing among His congregation, which matches this theme.

phrases.english: On the third day they would say:
"God stands in the congregation of God"
phrases.notes: תהלים פ״ב

phrases.english: because He revealed the land in His wisdom,
phrases.notes: The dry land appeared on day three

phrases.english: and prepared the world for His congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of daily psalms
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Tuesday the לוים sang ״אלהים נצב בעדת אל״, recalling the revealing of dry land for mankind.

steps.title: Wednesday's psalm: God of vengeance
steps.stepSummary: On Wednesday the לוים sang ״אל נקמות ה׳″. On the fourth day God created the sun and moon, and in the future He will punish those who worship them.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourth day they would say: "God of vengeance, the Lord," because He created the sun and moon, and in the future He will punish those who worship them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives Wednesday's psalm and its reason. The list continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On day four God made the sun and moon. Later, people would wrongly worship them, which is עבודה זרה. The psalm of vengeance looks ahead to God punishing those idol worshippers.
steps.confusionAlert: The reason here is different from the first three days. It does not only praise what was created that day. It looks to the future, when God will punish people who misuse that creation by worshipping it.

phrases.english: On the fourth day they would say:
"God of vengeance, the Lord"
phrases.notes: תהלים צ״ד

phrases.english: because He created the sun and moon,
and in the future will punish those who worship them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of daily psalms
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Wednesday the לוים sang ״אל נקמות ה׳″, recalling the creation of the sun and moon and the future punishment of their worshippers.

steps.title: Thursday's psalm: birds and fish praise God
steps.stepSummary: On Thursday the לוים sang ״הרנינו לאלהים עוזנו״, because on the fifth day God created birds and fish that praise Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fifth day they would say: 'Sing aloud to God our strength.' This is because on that day He created birds and fish to praise His name.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי עקיבא continues its list with Thursday's psalm and the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern stays the same: each psalm matches what God created on that day of Creation. Birds sing and fish fill the sea, so their creation fits a psalm that calls out to sing to God.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds and fish (created on the fifth day)

phrases.english: On the fifth day they would say:
'Sing aloud to God our strength' (Tehillim 81)
because He created birds and fish
to praise His name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's day-by-day list after Wednesday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thursday's psalm is ״הרנינו״, matching the creation of birds and fish.

steps.title: Friday's psalm: God finished and reigns
steps.stepSummary: On Friday the לוים sang ״ה׳ מלך גאות לבש״, because on the sixth day God completed His work and ruled over all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the sixth day they would say: 'ה׳ reigns, He is clothed in majesty.' This is because He finished His work and ruled over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with Friday's psalm and its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once Creation was complete on the sixth day, God's kingship over a finished world was fully shown. That is why the psalm about God reigning fits Friday.

phrases.english: On the sixth day they would say:
'ה׳ reigns, He is clothed in majesty' (Tehillim 93)
because He completed His work
and ruled over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next day in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Friday's psalm is ״ה׳ מלך״, because God finished Creation and reigned over it.

steps.title: שבת's psalm: the future day that is all שבת
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the לוים sang ״מזמור שיר ליום השבת״. According to רבי עקיבא, this refers to the future world, a 'day that is entirely שבת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the seventh day they would say: 'A psalm, a song for the day of שבת.' This means the day that is entirely שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the שבת psalm. Unlike the other six, he explains it as referring to the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first six reasons all describe what God did during Creation, which is the past. Here the reason suddenly points to the future: a time when the whole world is 'שבת,' meaning at rest. This switch is exactly what רבי נחמיה will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: For the day that is entirely שבת (the future world)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'a day that is all שבת' as just the regular weekly שבת. רבי עקיבא means a future era, which is why רבי נחמיה objects.

phrases.english: On the seventh day they would say:
'A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbat' (Tehillim 92)
for the day that is entirely Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Refers to the future world, according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list, but changes the type of reason from past to future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת psalm refers to the future 'day that is all שבת'.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה questions why שבת is treated differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה asks why the חכמים would split the psalms, making six about the past and one about the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: What did the חכמים see that made them divide between these psalms?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי עקיבא's explanation of the שבת psalm. This sets up his own alternative reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has the form of a question, but it works as an objection. A consistent list should give the same kind of reason for every day. Switching only שבת to the future breaks the pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they see (why did they decide)?

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said:
What did the Sages see
to distinguish between these chapters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's future-based reason for the שבת psalm.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is inconsistent for six reasons to be about the past and one to be about the future.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה keeps the first six reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה restates the reasons for days one through six exactly as רבי עקיבא gave them, all about Creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: on the first day, because He acquired, gave over, and ruled in His world. On the second, because He divided His works and reigned over them. On the third, because He revealed land in His wisdom and prepared the world for His people. On the fourth, because He created sun and moon and will punish those who worship them. On the fifth, because He created birds and fish to praise His name. On the sixth, because He completed His work and reigned over them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה begins his own version with 'אלא' (rather). He first repeats the six weekday reasons that he agrees with, which sets up his change for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing changes for days one through six. The repetition shows that he agrees with all of them. It lays out the past-based pattern that the seventh day will now match.

phrases.english: Rather: on the first day, because He acquired and transferred
and was ruler in His world.
On the second, because He divided His works
and reigned over them.
On the third, because He revealed land in His wisdom
and prepared the world for His congregation.
On the fourth, because He created sun and moon
and in the future will punish those who worship them.
On the fifth, because He created birds and fish
to praise His name.
On the sixth, because He completed His work
and reigned over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts רבי נחמיה's answer to his own objection by restating the agreed six reasons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reading that makes all seven reasons consistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Days one through six stay as רבי עקיבא explained them.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: שבת's psalm is because God rested
steps.stepSummary: For the seventh day, רבי נחמיה explains the psalm as referring to the past: God rested on the first Shabbat of Creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the seventh day, because He rested.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי נחמיה's real change. The שבת psalm is about God resting after Creation, not about the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now all seven reasons describe what God did during the week of Creation, so the pattern is consistent. The only point of disagreement with רבי עקיבא is this seventh reason.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא says the שבת psalm is about the future 'day that is all שבת.' רבי נחמיה says it is about the past, when God rested after Creation.

phrases.english: On the seventh, because He rested.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי נחמיה's list with his new שבת reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שבת psalm refers to a future era (רבי עקיבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The שבת psalm refers to God's rest at Creation, which keeps all seven reasons about the past.

steps.title: The dispute depends on רב קטינא: one thousand years of destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two תנאים disagree over רב קטינא's view. He holds that the world lasts six thousand years and is then destroyed for one thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree about the view of רב קטינא. רב קטינא said: The world will exist for six thousand years, and for one thousand it will be destroyed, as it says: 'And ה׳ alone will be exalted on that day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי נחמיה is really based on, starting with רב קטינא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'day' for God is a thousand years. If the destruction lasts one thousand years, that is like a single seventh 'day' of rest after six. This fits רבי עקיבא's 'day that is all שבת.'

phrases.english: And they disagree regarding the statement of Rav Ketina,
as Rav Ketina said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיתָּא אַלְפֵי שְׁנֵי הָוֵה עָלְמָא וְחַד חָרוּב,
phrases.english: The world will exist six thousand years, and one thousand it will be destroyed,
as it says: 'And ה׳ alone will be exalted on that day' (Yeshayahu 2).
phrases.notes: 'That day' is a single day, and one divine day is a thousand years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the root of the רבי עקיבא and רבי נחמיה dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב קטינא, the world is destroyed for one thousand years, which matches רבי עקיבא's single future 'שבת'.

steps.title: אביי: two thousand years of destruction
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that the destruction lasts two thousand years. On this view the future cannot be a single 'שבת day,' which fits רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Two thousand years it will be destroyed, as it says: 'He will revive us after two days.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the other view, which explains why רבי נחמיה would not read the שבת psalm as being about the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two 'days' of destruction do not match one שבת day. So someone who holds like אביי cannot connect the שבת psalm to the future, and must say it refers to God resting at Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב קטינא
He will revive us after two days

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a disagreement about the meaning of a psalm can depend on a deeper disagreement about how long the world will be destroyed.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Two thousand it will be destroyed,
as it says: 'He will revive us after two days' (Hoshea 6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב קטינא, which lines up with רבי נחמיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, the destruction lasts two thousand years, so there is no single future 'שבת day'.

steps.title: What was sung at the שבת מוסף offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which song the לויים sang over the קרבן מוסף of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the extra offerings of שבת, what did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. We already know the daily psalm for each day of the week, so now it asks what the לויים sang over the extra שבת offering. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the regular daily שיר of the morning תמיד. On שבת there is also a קרבן מוסף, which needs its own song. The גמרא wants to know what that song was.

phrases.english: At the additional offerings of Shabbat
what would they recite?
phrases.notes: The subject is the לויים singing in the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the daily psalms (and the מחלוקת about the seventh-day psalm) to the special שבת מוסף song.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the song sung over the שבת מוסף.

steps.title: רב: האזינו, divided by the memory-word הזיו לך
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the לויים sang שירת האזינו, split into six sections marked by הזי״ו ל״ך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן בר רבא said in the name of רב: 'הזיו לך.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. He gives a short memory-word whose six letters mark the six sections of שירת האזינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter is the first letter of one section: ה (האזינו), ז (זכור), י (ירכיבהו), ו (וירא), ל (לולי), כ (כי ידין). So the שבת מוסף song was שירת האזינו, divided into six parts.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory-word (סימן) for the six opening words of the parts of האזינו
משה's song in דברים פרק ל״ב
A memory-aid made from letters or words

steps.confusionAlert: הזיו לך is not a word with a meaning here. It is only a list of six first letters, one for each section of האזינו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Anan bar Rava said that Rav said:
Hei, zayin, yod, vav, lamed, kaf.
phrases.notes: These are the first letters of the six sections of האזינו: האזינו, זכור, ירכיבהו, וירא, לולי, כי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שבת מוסף song is שירת האזינו in six sections: הזי״ו ל״ך.

steps.title: The same division is used for the קריאת התורה in the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רב adds that האזינו is split into the same six parts when it is read in the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: Just as the song is divided here, so it is divided in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching of רב links the בית המקדש practice to shul. When האזינו is read as the קריאת התורה, the עליות break at the same six places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a practical rule for today. The places where the לויים stopped in the מקדש are also the stopping points between the people called up to the תורה for פרשת האזינו.

keyTerms.meaning: In the way they are divided here (in the מקדש)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for how the עליות of פרשת האזינו are divided in shul today.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥanan bar Rava said that Rav said:
In the manner that they are divided here (in the Temple),
so too are they divided in the synagogue.
phrases.notes: This refers to the sections of the קריאת התורה of האזינו.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related rule based on the six-part division just given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six-part division of האזינו used in the מקדש is also used for the קריאת התורה in the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: What was sung at the שבת afternoon offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which song the לויים sang over the afternoon תמיד on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the afternoon offering of שבת, what did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a parallel question, this time about the שבת afternoon (מנחה) offering. This line sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every day has an afternoon תמיד. The question is whether שבת afternoon had a special song of its own, just as the מוסף did.

phrases.english: At the afternoon offering of Shabbat
what would they recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question as step 14, applied to a different offering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The song sung over the שבת afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: שירת הים and שירת הבאר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says they sang אז ישיר and מי כמוך (the two halves of שירת הים), and אז ישיר of שירת הבאר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'Then sang' (משה), and 'Who is like You,' and 'Then sang' (Israel).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers with three sections. Two are halves of שירת הים, and the third is שירת הבאר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first אז ישיר is שמות ט״ו:א, and מי כמוך begins its second half (ט״ו:יא). The second אז ישיר is במדבר כ״א:יז, the Song of the Well. So the מנחה song has three parts, while the מוסף song has six. That number difference matters in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Then sang', the opening of a song
'Who is like You', the second half of שירת הים
The Song of the Well (במדבר כ״א)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase אז ישיר appears twice, but it refers to two different songs. The first is שירת הים in שמות. The second is שירת הבאר in במדבר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
'Then sang (Moses),' and 'Who is like You,'
phrases.notes: These are the two halves of שירת הים.

phrases.english: and 'Then sang (Israel).'
phrases.notes: This is שירת הבאר, במדבר כ״א:יז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מנחה song is three sections: אז ישיר, מי כמוך, and the אז ישיר of the Well.

steps.title: All the sections in one שבת, or one section per שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether all the sections were sung on a single שבת, or one section each week.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Were all of these said on one שבת, or perhaps on each שבת they said one?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the songs, the גמרא asks how they were scheduled. Did the לויים sing all the sections every שבת, or only one section each שבת in a rotating cycle?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real open question (איבעיא), not an attack on anyone. Both options are possible. Either the whole song was sung each week, or the sections rotated over several weeks.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised to them (a real open question)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי כּוּלְּהוּ בְּחַד שַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Do they recite all of these on one Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֹּל שַׁבְּתָא וְשַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי חַד?
phrases.english: or perhaps on each and every Shabbat they recite one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the sections from steps 15 and 18 were scheduled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the sections were all sung each שבת or rotated one per שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's ברייתא: the second set cycles twice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי: by the time the first set finishes once, the second set has gone around twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי יוסי said: By the time the first one says its cycle once, the second goes back around twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. רבי יוסי compares the two sets of songs: the six-part מוסף set and the three-part מנחה set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every section were sung every שבת, both sets would finish every week and neither would 'repeat twice' while the other finished once. The only way to make sense of this is one section per שבת. Then six weeks complete the מוסף set, while the three-part מנחה set finishes twice in that time.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei said:
By the time the first (set) recites once,
phrases.notes: The first set is the six-part מוסף song.

phrases.english: the second (set) repeats twice.
phrases.notes: The second set is the three-part מנחה song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle the question of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The view that one section was sung each שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי: six parts against three parts, so the second set completes two cycles while the first completes one.

steps.title: Conclusion: one section each שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that each שבת only one section was sung.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: each and every שבת they said one. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from רבי יוסי's ברייתא and confirms it. The songs rotated, with one section each שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'twice versus once' language only works with a rotating schedule. So the question of step 19 is settled: the מוסף song took six weeks to complete, and the מנחה song took three.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a source)

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת the לויים sang האזינו (six parts, הזי״ו ל״ך) at מוסף, and שירת הים and שירת הבאר (three parts) at מנחה. They sang one part each שבת, so the מנחה cycle ran twice for every single מוסף cycle.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כׇּל שַׁבְּתָא וְשַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי חַד,
phrases.english: Learn from here that each and every Shabbat they recite one (section);
indeed, learn from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כׇּל שַׁבְּתָא וְשַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each שבת, only one section of each song was sung, in a rotating cycle.

steps.title: The Divine Presence left in ten stages, and the Sanhedrin was exiled in ten stages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the שכינה left in ten journeys, proven from פסוקים. The סנהדרין was exiled in ten matching stages, known by tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אידי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The שכינה traveled ten journeys, and we know this from verses. Matching them, the סנהדרין went into exile ten times, and we know this from tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a teaching of רבי יוחנן. The teaching has two parallel halves: the שכינה left in ten stages, and the סנהדרין was exiled in ten stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves rest on two different kinds of source. The journeys of the שכינה are proven from פסוקים (מקראי). The exiles of the סנהדרין come from a received tradition (מגמרא). The word וכנגדן tells us the two lists match each other step for step.
steps.confusionAlert: Here מגמרא does not mean 'from our גמרא text.' It means a tradition handed down from teacher to student, as opposed to something proven from a פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section. The גמרא will now prove the ten journeys of the שכינה one by one, and then turn to the ten exiles of the סנהדרין.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Idi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The Divine Presence traveled ten journeys, as known from verses,
phrases.notes: These stages happened at the time of the destruction of the first בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and corresponding to them the Sanhedrin was exiled, as known from tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the שבת songs of the לויים ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה left in ten stages, proven from פסוקים. The סנהדרין was exiled in ten matching stages, known from tradition.

steps.title: The list of the ten journeys of the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists all ten stages: from the כפורת, through the בית המקדש and the city, out to the wilderness, and finally back up to Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שכינה traveled ten journeys, known from verses: from the כפורת to a כרוב, from one כרוב to the other כרוב, from the כרוב to the threshold, from the threshold to the courtyard, from the courtyard to the מזבח, from the מזבח to the roof, from the roof to the wall, from the wall to the city, from the city to a mountain, from the mountain to the wilderness. From the wilderness it went up and rested in its place, as it says: 'I will go and return to My place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first half of רבי יוחנן's teaching and spells out the ten stages in order. It ends with a פסוק showing that the שכינה finally returned to Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The path moves step by step from the holiest spot (the כפורת in the קודש הקדשים) outward and away from the people. The final stage, going up to 'its place,' shows the שכינה pulling away from the world completely. Each stage will now be proven from its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold cover on top of the ארון
One of the two golden cherubs on the כפורת
'I will go and return to My place' (הושע ה:טו)

steps.whatToRemember: The order is: כפורת → כרוב → כרוב → מפתן → חצר → מזבח → גג → חומה → עיר → הר → מדבר → back to Heaven.

phrases.english: The Divine Presence traveled ten journeys, as known from verses:
from the Ark cover to the cherub, and from one cherub to the other cherub,
and from the cherub to the threshold, and from the threshold to the courtyard,
and from the courtyard to the altar, and from the altar to the roof,
and from the roof to the wall, and from the wall to the city,
and from the city to a mountain, and from the mountain to the wilderness,
and from the wilderness it ascended and rested in its place,
phrases.notes: Its place in Heaven, apart from people.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'I will go and return to My place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the first half of רבי יוחנן's statement in order to explain it, listing the ten stages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten stages are כפורת, כרוב, כרוב, מפתן, חצר, מזבח, גג, חומה, עיר, הר, and מדבר, and then the שכינה returned to Heaven.

steps.title: Proof for the first stages: Ark cover, cherub, cherub, threshold
steps.stepSummary: Three פסוקים prove the first stages: the שכינה spoke from the כפורת, rested on one כרוב, and rose from the כרוב to the threshold.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the כפורת to a כרוב, from one כרוב to the other, and from the כרוב to the threshold, as it is written: 'I will meet with you there and speak with you from above the כפורת.' And it is written: 'He rode on a כרוב and flew.' And it is written: 'The glory of the God of Israel went up from the כרוב it was on to the threshold of the House.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts proving the list from step 23. Here it brings three פסוקים for the first stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows the starting point: the שכינה was above the כפורת. The second shows the שכינה could rest on a single כרוב, so it moved from the כפורת onto one כרוב and then to the other. The third פסוק, from יחזקאל, shows it leaving the כרוב for the threshold.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He rode upon a cherub' (שמואל ב כב:יא)
The threshold of the House (יחזקאל ט:ג)

phrases.aramaic: מִכַּפּוֹרֶת לִכְרוּב, מִכְּרוּב לִכְרוּב, וּמִכְּרוּב לְמִפְתָּן —
phrases.english: From the Ark cover to the cherub, from one cherub to the other cherub, and from the cherub to the threshold:
as it is written: 'And there I will meet with you,'
'and I will speak with you from above the Ark cover,'
phrases.notes: שמות כה:כב. This shows the starting point.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And He rode upon a cherub and flew,'
phrases.notes: The שכינה can rest on one כרוב alone.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וּכְבוֹד אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲלָה מֵעַל הַכְּרוּב
phrases.english: and it is written: 'And the glory of the God of Israel had ascended from the cherub'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עָלָיו אֶל מִפְתַּן הַבָּיִת״.
phrases.english: 'on which it was, to the threshold of the House.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכַּפּוֹרֶת לִכְרוּב, מִכְּרוּב לִכְרוּב, וּמִכְּרוּב לְמִפְתָּן — דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving, one stage at a time, the list given in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: Stages 1 to 3: כפורת to כרוב, כרוב to כרוב, and כרוב to מפתן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות כה:כב; שמואל ב כב:יא; יחזקאל ט:ג

steps.title: Proof for the move from the threshold to the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יחזקאל shows the courtyard filled with the brightness of God's glory.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the threshold to the courtyard, as it is written: 'The House was filled with the cloud, and the courtyard was full of the brightness of God's glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the next stage on the list, the move from the threshold out to the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the glory now shone in the courtyard, outside the building. This shows the שכינה had moved past the threshold into the חצר.

phrases.english: And from the threshold to the courtyard, as it is written:
'And the House was filled with the cloud,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶחָצֵר מָלְאָה אֶת נֹגַהּ כְּבוֹד ה׳״.
phrases.english: 'and the courtyard was full of the brightness of the Lord's glory.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל י:ד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proofs with the next stage.

steps.title: Proofs for the moves to the altar and to the roof
steps.stepSummary: עמוס shows God standing on the מזבח. משלי, about sitting on the corner of a roof, shows the move to the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the courtyard to the מזבח, as it is written: 'I saw God standing on the מזבח.' From the מזבח to the roof, as it is written: 'It is better to sit on the corner of a roof.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves two more stages: from the courtyard to the מזבח, and from the מזבח up to the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in עמוס places the שכינה on the מזבח, which stands in the courtyard. The פסוק in משלי is read as a hint that the שכינה went to a corner of the roof of the בית המקדש. On this reading, it preferred the roof to staying inside with a 'quarrelsome' people.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק in משלי is plainly about a person and a quarrelsome wife. The גמרא reads it as a hint about the שכינה, which is not the פסוק's simple meaning.

phrases.english: From the courtyard to the altar, as it is written:
'I saw the Lord standing on the altar.'
phrases.notes: עמוס ט:א

phrases.english: And from the altar to the roof, as it is written:
'It is better to dwell in a corner of the roof.'
phrases.notes: משלי כא:ט. The verse continues: 'than in a house with a quarrelsome woman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proofs with stages 5 and 6.
steps.raayaObject: Stages 5 and 6: חצר to מזבח, and מזבח to גג.

steps.title: Proofs for the moves to the wall and to the city
steps.stepSummary: עמוס shows God standing on a wall. מיכה shows God's voice calling to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the roof to the wall, as it is written: 'And behold, God was standing on a wall made with a plumb line.' From the wall to the city, as it is written: 'God's voice calls to the city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves two more stages: from the roof to the wall, and from the wall out into the city. The proofs for the last stages (mountain and wilderness) come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק places the שכינה one step farther from the קודש הקדשים: first on the wall of הר הבית, then in the city of ירושלים itself. The list is not finished yet, since the הר and מדבר stages still need proofs.

keyTerms.meaning: A wall built straight with a plumb line (עמוס ז:ז)

phrases.english: From the roof to the wall, as it is written:
'And behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumb line.'
phrases.notes: עמוס ז:ז

phrases.english: From the wall to the city, as it is written:
'The Lord's voice cries to the city.'
phrases.notes: מיכה ו:ט

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proofs with stages 7 and 8.
steps.raayaObject: Stages 7 and 8: גג to חומה, and חומה to עיר.

steps.title: From the city to the mountain, and from the mountain to the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים prove the next two stages: the שכינה rose from the city to the mountain east of it, and then moved from the mountain into the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the city to the mountain, as it is written: 'And the glory of ה׳ went up from the midst of the city and stood on the mountain east of the city.' And from the mountain to the wilderness, as it is written: 'It is better to dwell in a wilderness land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through its list of ten stages and gives a פסוק for stages nine and ten: city to mountain, then mountain to wilderness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל says outright that God's glory left the city and stood on the mountain to the east. The פסוק in משלי ends 'than with a quarreling, angry woman.' The hint is that the שכינה would rather sit in the wilderness than stay with a quarrelsome ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Mountain, here the mountain east of the city (הר הזיתים)
The glory of ה׳, meaning His Presence

phrases.english: And from the city to the mountain, as it is written:
"And the glory of ה׳ went up from the midst of the city
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 11:23

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּעֲמֹד עַל הָהָר אֲשֶׁר מִקֶּדֶם לָעִיר״.
phrases.english: and stood upon the mountain which is east of the city."
phrases.notes: This is הר הזיתים, the mountain closest to the מקדש.

phrases.english: And from the mountain to the wilderness, as it is written:
"It is better to dwell in a wilderness land."
phrases.notes: משלי 21:19. The verse goes on: 'than with a quarreling and angry woman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proofs for the list of stages, picking up right after the city.
steps.raayaObject: Stages 9 and 10 of the שכינה's departure: city to mountain, and mountain to wilderness

steps.title: From the wilderness back up to Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The last stage: the שכינה went up from the wilderness and returned to its place in Heaven, as the פסוק in הושע says, 'I will go and return to My place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the wilderness it went up and settled in its place, as it is written: 'I will go and return to My place, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the ten journeys (the last was mountain to wilderness), the גמרא proves the final ascent: the שכינה left the world completely and went back to Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'My place' is read as God's place in Heaven. The rest of the פסוק says 'until they admit their guilt.' That ending shows the door stays open: the שכינה will come back if ישראל does תשובה. This completes the list of ten stages.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for וגומר, 'and so on'; the rest of the פסוק is meant

steps.whatToRemember: The ten stages run along this path: כפורת, one כרוב, the other כרוב, the threshold, the courtyard, the מזבח, the roof, the wall, the city, the mountain, the wilderness, and then back to Heaven. Each stage is a step further away, as if the שכינה left slowly and unwillingly.

phrases.english: And from the wilderness it went up and settled in its place,
as it is written: "I will go and return to My place, etc."
phrases.notes: הושע 5:15. The verse continues: 'until they acknowledge their guilt.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for the final stage and closes the list of ten.
steps.raayaObject: Final stage: from the wilderness back to Heaven

steps.title: The שכינה waited six months in the wilderness for תשובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the שכינה waited in the wilderness for six months, hoping ישראל would do תשובה. When they did not, it said 'let them despair,' as the פסוק in איוב says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For six months the שכינה waited for ישראל in the wilderness, in case they would do תשובה. Once they did not return, it said: 'Let them despair (be lost),' as it says: 'And the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape is lost to them, and their hope is a sigh of the soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a detail to the wilderness stage: it was not a quick stop. The שכינה waited there six months, giving ישראל a chance to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why there was a stage in the wilderness at all: it was a last waiting period before leaving the world. Only after ישראל failed to repent did the שכינה give up. The words 'תיפח עצמן' (let them despair) connect to the words 'מפח נפש' (a sigh of the soul) in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them despair and be lost (literally, 'let their bones blow away')
A sigh or breathing-out of the soul, meaning despair

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even while leaving, the שכינה held back and gave ישראל time to return. This matches the hopeful ending of the הושע פסוק in the previous step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For six months the Divine Presence waited
for Israel in the wilderness,
in case they would return in repentance.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא חָזְרוּ — אָמַר: תִּיפַּח עַצְמָן,
phrases.english: Once they did not return, it said: Let them despair,
as it is said: "And the eyes of the wicked will fail,
phrases.notes: איוב 11:20

phrases.english: and escape is lost from them,
and their hope is a sigh of the soul."
phrases.notes: 'מפח' is the source for the word 'תיפח' used above.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים נִתְעַכְּבָה שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail about the wilderness stage that was just proven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה waited six months in the wilderness hoping for תשובה, and only then left the world completely.

steps.title: The סנהדרין also went into exile in ten stages
steps.stepSummary: Matching the ten stages of the שכינה, the סנהדרין was exiled in ten stages, known from tradition. The first stages are: from לשכת הגזית to חנות, from חנות to ירושלים, and from ירושלים to יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And matching them, the סנהדרין was exiled, as known from tradition: from לשכת הגזית to חנות, and from חנות to ירושלים, and from ירושלים to יבנה,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new list that parallels the first one: just as the שכינה left in ten stages, the סנהדרין moved away from its home in ten stages. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list does not come from פסוקים. It comes from a received tradition (גמרא). The סנהדרין's proper seat was לשכת הגזית inside the מקדש area. Each move took it farther away: first to חנות on הר הבית, then into the city of ירושלים, and then out of ירושלים to יבנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And matching them, parallel to them
From a received tradition, not from a פסוק
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, the סנהדרין's seat in the מקדש
A place on הר הבית, outside the main מקדש area
Yavne, the town where the סנהדרין moved after leaving ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word 'מִגְּמָרָא' does not mean 'from the Talmud.' It means 'from a received tradition,' passed down from teacher to student rather than learned from a פסוק.

phrases.english: And corresponding to them the Sanhedrin was exiled, known from tradition:
from the Chamber of Hewn Stone to Chanut,
and from Chanut to Jerusalem,
and from Jerusalem to Yavne,
